Last year, the former Greater Manchester mayor even said spades could be in the ground by 2028 Now Mr Burnham sits in Downing Street as Prime Minister, his successor in the city-region, Bev Craig, hasn’t mentioned the project. She did speak about the expansion of the tram network to Stockport in her manifesto, but Heywood was omitted Despite this, Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM) has confirmed they are working on a business case for the Heywood project. It falls under what TfGM calls the Oldham-Rochdale-Heywood-Bury Tram-Train pathfinder The new Metrolink line would connect Bury to Rochdale via Heywood and then loop back through Shaw towards Oldham . However, no plans have been formally approved When opened, the scheme would give Greater Manchester two Metrolink firsts: The first ‘orbital’ Metrolink route, i.e. one which does not go via the city centre, and the first ‘tram-train’, set to be rolled out across the city in coming years

input.evidence_text: Manchester canal lost for 91 years after gigantic breach is set to resurface within months A new cafe and canoe and kayak school will be features of the restored length of waterway Comments News Chris Gee Local democracy reporter 07:11, 31 Aug 2026 Vi A section of canal lost since it collapsed 90 years ago is set to be ‘in water’ and enjoyed by the public within months. Part of the Manchester, Bolton and Bury canal near Little Lever was breached in July 1936 Millions of gallons of water from the channel came cascading down into the River Irwell below. The gigantic breach happened close to the Nob End locks, on the canal’s arm towards Bury, with the affected section never restored But work done by Watson Homes, who are building a new 255 home estate alongside the affected waterway at the former Creams Mill site in Little Lever, is set to change that Watson has been restoring a 800 metre section of the waterway as part of the planning permission. The extensive work means the section of canal is set to be ‘in water’ by May 2027 The new section of waterway will also create a destination for visitors as a new café is planned alongside a canoe and kayaking school

The gigantic breach happened close to the Nob End locks, on the canal’s arm towards Bury, with the affected section never restored But work done by Watson Homes, who are building a new 255 home estate alongside the affected waterway at the former Creams Mill site in Little Lever, is set to change that Watson has been restoring a 800 metre section of the waterway as part of the planning permission.
